stories.notes: Complex cross-market (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature with no acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Needs openspec to elaborate AC and technical depth first, then speckit to harden testability, security, and edge cases.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests Live Preview of Content in CMS — a genuinely new capability. No existing preview mechanism appears in the indexed codebase. The central integration point is useContent (236+ callers), which is where preview-mode content delivery must plug in so every consumer gets live updates without individual changes. Acceptance criteria are empty; VCs derived solely from the description.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria list with a note identifying useContent as the central integration point. I derived all ACs from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the GO/UP/MX brand scope, and the listed file paths (useContent.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, contentstack.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts). Key additions: (1) AC-5/AC-6 cover error-handling edge cases (invalid token, API failure) not mentioned by openspec; (2) AC-7/AC-8 explicitly cover ContentstackLink and contentCard rendering in preview since those files were called out; (3) AC-9 addresses cross-brand isolation for GO/UP/MX; (4) AC-10 ensures context-level integration so 236+ useContent consumers don't each need changes; (5) AC-11 adds a visible preview indicator — critical UX so editors know they're viewing draft; (6) AC-12 covers nested/rich-text content resolution; (7) AC-13 covers accessibility; (8) AC-14 covers rapid-update debouncing. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents, so these ACs are based on file names and standard Contentstack live-preview patterns. If useContent or ContentstackContext already have partial preview support, some ACs may need adjustment after code review.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed non-overlapping value: openspec identified useContent (236+ callers) as the central integration point, and speckit derived 14 acceptance criteria covering edge cases (error handling, cross-brand isolation, accessibility, debouncing) that openspec did not address. However, the overall quality is undermined by a critical gap: neither agent inspected actual file contents. Openspec added zero acceptance criteria despite the story having an empty AC list — it stopped at integration-point identification. Speckit then derived all 14 ACs speculatively from the story title, file names, and standard Contentstack live-preview patterns, explicitly admitting it could not read the files. This means the ACs are pattern-based assumptions, not grounded in codebase reality. If useContent or ContentstackContext already has partial preview support, multiple ACs may be redundant or incorrect. Human review is required to validate ACs against actual code before implementation.
